title_prefix: A miniscript descriptor's node reports s
mechanism: make-ms-node (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:586-592) sets script-size to (length (ms-node-script node)) only when every key in the node is already a byte sequence, and to 0 otherwise. Inside a descriptor *ms-key-parser* is bound (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:897-911) so every key is a desc-key STRUCT, never a sequence, and every node of every miniscript descriptor therefore reports script-size 0. ms-node-valid-p (:623-634) then evaluates 0 <= 3600, which is always true, so the MaxScriptSize half of Core's IsValid is dead for exactly the inputs that reach the RPC; the ops and stack limits still work because they are computed from the tree shape, so IsSane passes too. Core enforces the bound twice and never looks at key bytes: internal::Parse carries a running script_size accumulated from the FRAGMENT SHAPE (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:1865 for the initial 1, :1898-1906 for multi/multi_a, :1960-2090 per fragment) and bails with {} the moment it exceeds internal::MaxScriptSize(ctx) -- checked at the top of the parse loop (:1912) and again per wrapper character (:1931) -- and Node::IsValid re-checks ScriptSize() <= MaxScriptSize afterwards (:1670-1673).
consequence: getdescriptorinfo, deriveaddresses and importdescriptors accept a wsh(<miniscript>) descriptor whose real witnessScript exceeds MAX_STANDARD_P2WSH_SCRIPT_SIZE, which Core refuses outright at Parse; the node then derives addresses from it and receives to them, while any spend is non-standard (our own IsWitnessStandard, src/validation/transaction.lisp:476, rejects a witnessScript over +max-standard-p2wsh-script-size+ 3600) so the spending transaction will not relay. The coins are not consensus-locked -- a miner could include such a transaction -- so this is a wrong answer an operator acts on rather than outright loss, hence S2 rather than S1. The same hole disables the 329482-byte tapscript ceiling for tr() leaves, since a tr() leaf's node is built through the same key-expression parser.
evidence: Container: /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s2, warm image, build/ga11probe/p2.lisp, p2b.lisp, p2c.lisp. Test expression: and_v-chained multi(1,<20 distinct derived pubkeys>) fragments, six of them, 8138 characters. (a) LITERAL keys (positive control that the gate works at all): bl.val:ms-parse -> script-size 4104, real script length 4104, ms-node-valid-p NIL, ms-node-sane-p NIL. Five multis (6780 chars): script-size 3420, valid-p T, sane-p T -- so the gate discriminates. (b) The SAME expression inside wsh() as a descriptor: parse-descriptor accepted, node script-size 0, ms-node-valid-p T, ms-node-sane-p T, real witnessScript 4104 bytes, scriptPubKey 002086683a41096d2d11d8fb70389849335d5303b455b7ed4ccc5e475546dd0006f0. The five-multi (3420-byte) descriptor reports the identical 0/T/T, so acceptance carries no information about size. (c) Through bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method: getdescriptorinfo -> issolvable T; deriveaddresses -> bcrt1qse5r5sgfd5k3rk8mwqufsjfnt4fs8dz4klk5enz7ga25dhgqqmcqfgw8es; importdescriptors into a watch-only wallet -> success T for BOTH the over-3600 and the under-3600 descriptor. (d) Core's verdict on the same string, computed by hand from miniscript.h's per-fragment sizes: script_size starts at 1 (:1865); each multi(1,20 keys) adds 2 + (20>16) + (1>16) + 34*20 = 683 (:1905); each of the five and_v adds 1 (:2072); total 1 + 5 + 6*683 = 4104 > MaxScriptSize 3600 -> Parse returns {} at :1912. The arithmetic is exact: our measured real script is 4104 bytes, and the five-multi form computes to 1 + 4 + 5*683 = 3420, matching its measured 3420 and passing Core's bound. (Core's ComputeScriptLen gives MULTI = 1 + BuildScript(20).size()=2 + BuildScript(1).size()=1 + 34*20 = 684 per fragment, and the Parse accumulator's one-byte-per-leaf borrow plus the leading 1 reconciles the two to the same 4104.) Sources: src/validation/miniscript.lisp:586-592, :595-596, :611-615, :623-634; the only reader of ms-node-script-size in the tree is :634.
fix_shape: Stop deriving the bound from generated bytes and port Core's shape-based accumulator. Give the parser a running script_size seeded at 1 that each fragment increments by Core's own constant (miniscript.h:1960-2090: 34 or 33 per pk_k key by context, 24 for pkh, 23 for pk_h, 38/26 for the hash fragments, 1 + BuildScript(k) for older/after, 2 + (n>16) + (k>16) + 34n for multi, (1+32+1)n + BuildScript(k) for multi_a, 5 for andor/and_n, 1/2/3/4 for the binary combinators, 2 + BuildScript(k) for thresh, and the per-character wrapper costs at :1931), compare it against ms-max-script-size at the top of the parse loop and inside the wrapper loop, and fail the parse there -- which also fixes the cubic cost of d722b087, since the two are the same missing mechanism. Keep make-ms-node's cached script-size as Core's Node::CalcScriptLen instead: ComputeScriptLen (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.cpp:265-296) derives a node's length in O(1) from its fragment, its first sub's type and the SUM of its subs' lengths, so it needs no key bytes at all and the descriptor/literal distinction disappears. A regression test must assert the descriptor form and the literal-key form of one over-limit expression agree, since that divergence is what hid this.
